This '''individual''' was a [[human]] who was present in the [[bar]] of [[Takodana Castle|Maz Kanata's castle]] on [[Takodana]] when the [[First Order]] [[Battle of Takodana|attacked]] the [[planet]]. They were seen talking to [[Grummgar]] as [[Finn]] left the castle with [[Sidon Ithano]] and [[Quiggold]]. Shortly afterward, they were one of the many people who witnessed the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|destruction]] of the [[Hosnian system]] from outside the castle.<ref name="VII" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You probably remember a really big monster. A gangster kind of dude who was an animatronic creation and the whole scene was supposed to be that I would have a fight with him; I was going to ask for my money and he was going to have a go at me. In the end we ran out of time to do it and it never got shot the way J.J. wanted to shoot it. There's a very brief scene of me trying to have an argument with him as Finn is leaving, and that's the only bit we got of it. We were running out of time and of course we weren't the principal part of the story at that point. J.J. wanted us involved and we were not supposed to be extras, we were supposed to be there playing characters, so he was really frustrated that we ran out of time.|[[Miltos Yerolemou]]|<ref name="Story">{{WebCite|url=https://theirstarwarsstories.com/2020/04/14/miltos-yerolemou-his-star-wars-story|text=Miltos Yerolemou – His Star Wars Story|date=April 14, 2020|archivedate=20220308155656}}</ref>}}
[[File:GrummarWithBarPatron.png|thumb|left|280px|The bar patron talking to Grummgar, in what was originally supposed to be a longer sequence]]

The bar patron was portrayed by British actor [[Miltos Yerolemou]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']].<ref name="VII" /> The actor did not audition for the role, but was cast when casting director [[Nina Gold]] sent his tape to director [[J.J. Abrams]], who was looking for character actors to play [[Realspace|space]] [[pirate]]s. Gold was familiar with the actor due to his work on ''[[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones|Game of Thrones]]'', for which she was also the casting director.<ref name="Story" />

Despite the character's short screen time, Yerolemou spent two weeks filming at [[Pinewood Studios]]. Due to the secrecy of the production, he received no script and wasn't told what he was going to do until he showed up for filming. Yerolemou wore orange plasters on his [[Limb|fingers]] and [[nose]] for the part, and had a tube going up his nose. He was told that they didn't have to do the tube, but the actor insisted that they keep it, saying that it was the best thing about the character's design.<ref name="Story" />
[[File:BarPatronCostumeTFA.jpg|thumb|right|170px|Yerolemou in costume for the part]]

Originally, the bar patron was going to have a bigger role in the film and was going to have a fight with the character [[Grummgar]], with the patron asking for his [[Currency|money]] and the hulking alien having a go at him. However, due to time constraints, all that was shot was a segment where the patron is trying to have an argument with Grummgar;<ref name="Story" /> this can be seen in the background of two shots where [[Finn]] is leaving [[Takodana Castle|Moz Kanata's castle]].<ref name="VII" /> Abrams intended for the patron and some of the other background characters to be involved in the story as opposed to merely being extras, and was frustrated that they ran out of time.<ref name="Story" />

For the bit that was kept, Abrams instructed Yerolemou to stand in front of the animatronic Grummgar: "You say something and he says something…in fact he's not going to say anything at all because we are going to dub it later." Because Grummgar was animatronic, with three people inside operating him, they did not rehearse the scene. The actor hadn't seen the creature move yet, so the first time they shot the scene, when the big alien started picking up a glass of [[brandy]], the actor forgot that the characters were supposed to be having an argument, and ruined the take by blurting out his amazement.<ref name="Story" /> However, in the actual film, Grummgar is merely seen holding the glass and no line is dubbed in.<ref name="VII" />
